questions.question: What is the molecular composition of a single molecule of carbon dioxide?
options: One carbon atom and one oxygen atom
Two carbon atoms and one oxygen atom
One carbon atom and two oxygen atoms
Two carbon atoms and two oxygen atoms

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of the Earth's atmosphere is made up of carbon dioxide?
Which of the following gases is classified as a greenhouse gas?
options: Nitrogen
Oxygen
Argon
Carbon dioxide

questions.question: What is the primary consequence of having too many greenhouse gases in the atmosphere?
options: An increase in average global temperature, known as global warming
A rapid decrease in the atmospheric pressure
The complete depletion of the ozone layer
An increase in the concentration of nitrogen gas

questions.question: What type of rock is coal, and why does it burn?
options: It is an igneous rock that burns because of trapped volcanic gases.
It is a sedimentary rock that burns because it is made mostly of carbon, with some impurities.
It is a metamorphic rock that burns due to high concentrations of sulfur.
It is a sedimentary rock that burns because it is composed entirely of pure liquid hydrocarbons.

questions.question: From what material does coal originally form over millions of years?
options: Deep sediments of organic matter made of prehistoric plants
Volcanic ash layers mixed with molten lava
Mineral deposits from ancient saltwater lakes
Decomposed skeletons of prehistoric marine reptiles

questions.question: How did oil and natural gas form millions of years ago?
options: From the compression of giant prehistoric forest trees
From dead plankton mixed in with sediments
From volcanic eruptions under high atmospheric pressure
From the accumulation of wind-blown desert sands

questions.question: Where exactly are oil and natural gas located underground?
options: In massive hollow caves within metamorphic rock
In the pores of sedimentary rock
Flowing freely as underground rivers between igneous rock layers
Trapped inside solid crystals of quartz and granite

questions.question: Which processes are responsible for the formation of sedimentary rock from buried sediment?
options: Melting by magma and subsequent rapid cooling at the surface
Intense heat and pressure that recrystallize minerals without melting
Compression of the sediment and cementation of grains by salts from fluids
The cooling and crystallization of dissolved minerals in open air

questions.question: What happens to bones buried in sedimentary rock over a very long period?
options: They are melted by geothermal heat into liquid calcium.
They are very slowly dissolved by water and replaced by minerals in the water.
They shrink and turn directly into natural gas within the rock pores.
They remain completely unchanged and do not interact with groundwater.

questions.question: What is the primary composition of Earth's atmosphere?
options: 50% Nitrogen and 50% Oxygen
78% Nitrogen and 21% Oxygen, with very small amounts of other gases and particles
78% Oxygen and 21% Carbon dioxide, with very small amounts of nitrogen
90% Nitrogen, 9% Oxygen, and 1% Water vapour

questions.question: What is the scientific test to confirm the presence of carbon dioxide gas?
options: It relights a glowing splint.
It burns with a squeaky pop sound.
It turns damp red litmus paper blue.
It forms a white precipitate that turns limewater milky.

questions.question: How does erosion differ from weathering?
options: Erosion is the chemical breakdown of rock, whereas weathering is the physical breakdown.
Erosion is the process that removes material from where bedrock has been broken down, whereas weathering happens 'in place'.
Erosion only occurs in oceans, while weathering only occurs on high mountaintops.
Erosion happens instantly, while weathering takes billions of years to start.

questions.question: What effect does combustion have on the gases in Earth's atmosphere?
options: It decreases the amount of nitrogen gas.
It increases the amount of carbon dioxide.
It increases the amount of oxygen gas.
It has no effect on atmospheric composition.

questions.question: Which of the following processes reduces the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
options: Respiration by animals
Combustion of fossil fuels
Photosynthesis by plants, phytoplankton and some bacteria
Decomposition of dead plants and animals
